notes:
Context: mid-market CCaaS provider; building a real-time agent assist layer for enterprise customers. Interested in Redwood for low-latency streaming suggestions + safe tool-calls into their stack (Zendesk + internal ticketing).

Key quoted needs / comments from call: "we need suggestions in-line at sub-200ms and confident tool-calling that never changes ticket routing without human ok". Security team: strict KMS + residency constraints; SOC2 + audit logs mandatory.

POC plan (agreed):
- Week 0: baseline latency measurements (synthetic + real call traces)
- Week 1: 7-day POC running streaming assistant on a 2-GPU dedicated pool; simulate 3x spike windows
- Week 2: integrate function-calls to ticketing + mock agent UI; validate guardrails and fallback to cached recommendations

Success metrics / acceptance criteria:
- p99 inference latency for streaming suggestions < 150ms (target) on peak concurrent agents
- sustained throughput: 250-400 requests/sec per zonal pool during spikes
- no unapproved tool-calls during 1M utterance test (guardrail audit)
- cost target: unit economics competitive with current provider (total TCO review)

Technical priorities / notes:
- Heavy use of prefix/KV caching (customer has repetitive intents)
- Need clear model routing: fast small LM for short suggestions, fallback to larger LM for escalation
- Observability: token-level cost/latency traces + per-route dashboards required for pilot
- They want automated canary + A/B rollout for model updates to avoid agent regressions

Risks / open questions:
- Unknown behavior under sudden 5x traffic spikes (peak 30 min windows) — ask Redwood about autoscale and burst guarantees for Dedicated
- Data residency: some enterprise customers require EU-only storage for transcripts
- Zendesk API rate limits and tool-calling idempotency handling
